title: Mirror-touch synesthesia — people who feel others' pain physically
voiceover: Some people can't watch someone get hit because they feel the punch themselves. Literally. It's called mirror-touch synesthesia. When they see someone else being touched — a hand on a shoulder, a stubbed toe, a kiss — their brain activates the touch response as if it happened to them. They feel it on their own body. About 1 in 50 people experience this. Most go their whole lives thinking they're just empathetic, until they realize that most people don't physically wince when someone else gets hurt. Their nerves don't know whose body it is. Follow Mindbloom for one fact a day.
